references.text: The sons of Manasseh and their clans are counted, forming the basis for the land distribution mentioned in Joshua 17:5.
The daughters of Zelophehad, who belonged to the tribe of Manasseh, received inheritance rights, affecting the ten portions given to Manasseh in addition to Gilead and Bashan.
The half-tribe of Manasseh receives Gilead and Bashan on the east side of the Jordan, mentioned separately from the ten portions on the west side.
Provisions for the inheritance of Zelophehad's daughters ensured that their inheritance remained within the tribe of Manasseh, related to the land distribution.
The half-tribe of Manasseh receives Bashan and parts of Gilead on the east side of the Jordan, separated from the inheritance west of the Jordan.
Describes the inheritance of the half-tribe of Manasseh on the east side of the Jordan, including Gilead and Bashan.
The context for verse 5, explaining that Gilead and Bashan went to Machir, while the other clans received the ten portions.
The half-tribe of Manasseh lived on the east side of the Jordan in Bashan, while the other half lived west of the Jordan.
